query: Across the retrieved papers, what methods do recursive language model systems use to aggregate information that exceeds a single context window, and how do they differ in where the aggregation happens?
rule: Grade 2 = the paper presents or evaluates a method for handling or aggregating information that exceeds one context window. Grade 1 = the paper analyses the limitation or measures effective context, without proposing an aggregation method. Judged from title and abstract of the corpus row; full-text reading not done.
caveat: A pilot for choosing (k, n), not the W2a instrument: one query, seven judgements, a single judge, abstract-level reading. Do not report nDCG from it; report recall@n of the judged set.
